::: {#sol-flatten}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
rows = images.reshape(-1, 64)
print(rows.shape, torch.equal(rows, torch.tensor(pixels)))
```

`reshape(-1, 64)` asks for rows of 64 and lets PyTorch work out the number of rows, the `-1`.
It reads the entries in order, last dimension fastest,
so each image's row 0 comes first, then its row 1, and so on,
which undoes the `reshape(-1, 8, 8)` of @sol-load-tensor.
`torch.equal` confirms that the shapes and every entry match.
The course overview's [remark on the two arrangements](course-overview.qmd#rem-grid-or-vector) says which models take which.

:::
